overview: This Senate resolution recognizes November 2025 as National Family Caregivers Month. It notes that about 63 million Americans provide unpaid care to relatives and loved ones who are aging, ill or disabled, often facing financial strain, exhaustion and isolation. It commends these caregivers, points to the 2022 National Strategy to Support Family Caregivers as a guide for better support, and encourages people to learn about caregiving and help those who do it. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on November 18, 2025. It is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
for: Supporters say the resolution recognizes the huge, often unseen work family caregivers do and calls attention to the support they need.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not provide caregivers any new financial help, leave or services.
